title: Spring property names follow record metadata
summary: A record component preserves its exact spelling. An additional getter of the same spelling has no backing field and follows bean naming.

change.description: A record component preserves its exact spelling. An additional getter of the same spelling has no backing field and follows bean naming.

notes: Pair one of three altered component names with one preserved record or bean accessor.
The captured original module and its dependencies are identified by SHA-256. The setup record retains build and historical regression evidence.

The record component getWidget() and the extra getter getWidget() have identical method spellings. Only the component retained that spelling on the fix. The transplanted historical test suite failed 9 of 18 on the parent and passed all 18 on the landed artifact.

First startup recheck (20261123-011836). On both original artifacts the checker constructs the annotation-cache segments and reference queues and resolves the caller's declared method from its class file. All four public properties next stop at the nine-entry IdentityHashMap constructor during ClassUtils startup for optional Kotlin discovery.

All four ordinary metadata claims reach Map.entrySet in ClassUtils.<clinit>:174 after nine wrapper/primitive entries. The separate lookup control uses ClassUtils as its sole recorded initializer root, binds its string-keyed HashMaps, then calls the unmodified Accessors entries and replays all six original names per JVM. All nine matching selectors verified and all three parent component violations replayed on the original JVM.

Both historical Property JARs now execute ClassUtils initialization from ordinary startup. The inverse and name lookups agree for every traversal order. Nine selectors proved and all three original parent component violations replayed individually. The four primary claims now have three establishments and one refutation.
